text:
alex_w: heads up — saw an odd spike where EMEA non-prod traffic started routing to us-east-1 for ~8m. latency up ~350ms for affected calls. I think it’s the fallback heuristics + locality weight decay behaving oddly. attaching quick notes.
maria_s: yikes. any idea what triggered the decay? infra event or config rollout?
devops-bot: alert: routing-anomaly detected (severity: medium) — increased cross-region fallbacks from region=eu to region=us-east between 1969991100-1969991380. affected-tenants: 3. metric: fallback_count.
jia_l: looking at routing logs — several requests hit fallback path because model-variant-compat check returned incompatible for the eu variant, then routing chose lowest-cost region which is us-east. The cost heuristic currently ignores customer_tier during fallback selection (this is the bug).
alex_w: oh — so a lower-cost region gets picked without honoring tier affinity. that would explain latency and poor UX for paying customers.
pm_erik: which tiers were affected? any SLA breaches we should notify about?
jia_l: affected were prod-tier=standard (not enterprise) for two customers and one internal test tenant. no formal SLA breach yet but P50 latency hit our internal SLO for standard.
sre_zoe: immediate mitigation: we should flip the fallback to prefer locality+tier affinity before cost. hotpatching a policy flag is fastest. follow-up: add a circuit-breaker to stop cross-region fallback surges.
maria_s: can we also add a telemetry panel showing fallback selection breakdown by reason (variant-incompat, quota, capacity)? ops people kept asking "why eu traffic left eu".
jia_l: agreed. also need to enrich logs with selected_policy_reason and matched_tier so we can trace selection chain. example quick config that is problematic now:

```
{
  "fallback_policy": "min_cost",
  "respect_tier": false,
  "locality_decay_seconds": 300
}
```

we should change to:

```
{
  "fallback_policy": "tiered_locality",
  "respect_tier": true,
  "locality_decay_seconds": 60,
  "max_cross_region_per_min": 5
}
```
alex_w: I'll publish a hotpatch to policy-store with the new policy, canary to 10% of requests for 20m, then 100% if stable. command I’ll run:

`rictl policy apply --file=hotfix/196999-policy.json --canary=0.1 --owner=alex_w`
pm_erik: please include a rollback playbook in the PR description — customer comms team may need a heads-up if we escalate.
sre_zoe: I'll wire an automatic rate limiter in the routing proxy as secondary guard: per-tenant cross-region allowance + quick kill switch. also adding alert for fallback_count_rate > 10/min.
maria_s: for dashboard — add panels: 'fallback_count by reason & region', 'route_locality_score distribution', 'tenant_cross_region_events'. put it on the runbook board.
jia_l: I'll push the telemetry enrichment change and a trace sample to the traces team. also adding a unit test that ensures fallback honors customer_tier when respect_tier=true.
devops-bot: job started: policy-apply-job (id=job_7892) by alex_w. status: running.
alex_w: canary is live on 10% now. initial 10m looks good — fallback_count down ~80% for canary traffic.
sre_zoe: good signal. rolling to 100% in 10m unless we see errors.
jia_l: PR opened: #4123 with telemetry and test. linking trace example in PR.
pm_erik: thanks. action items: 1) alex hotpatch + canary -> done/in-progress; 2) zoe add proxy rate limiter + alert; 3) jia telemetry + tests + PR; 4) maria dashboard panels + runbook update; 5) ops: notify impacted customers if we see regression. assign owners in the PR.
maria_s: adding dashboard tiles now, pinging #customer-ops for possible outreach list.
alex_w: keeping thread updated if anything pops. TL;DR: bug = fallback ignored tier affinity; fix = change policy to tiered_locality + proxy guard + telemetry. :thumbsup
